topic.name: Describing Properties of the Sine Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \sin x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

\[ \sin{x} = \sin{(x+2n\pi)} . \]

Substituting $n=-10$ into the right-hand-side gives

\begin{align*} \sin{x} = \sin{(x-20\pi)} . \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\sin{x} = \dfrac{\sqrt 5}{3},$ then $\sin{(x-20\pi)} = \dfrac{\sqrt 5}{3}.$

Finally, then \[ \sqrt{5}\sin(x-20\pi) = \sqrt 5 \left( \dfrac{\sqrt 5}{3} \right) = \dfrac 5 3. \]

example.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Sine Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \sin x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for any integer $n$ we have \[ \sin{x} = \sin(x+2n\pi). \]

Substituting $n=5$ into the right-hand-side gives \begin{align*} \sin{x} = \sin(x+10\pi). \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\sin{x} = -\dfrac{5}{6},$ then $\sin(x+10\pi) = -\dfrac{5}{6}.$

Finally, then \begin{align} -\sin(x+10\pi)+2 & = -\left(-\dfrac 56\right) +2\\[5pt] & = \dfrac 56 +2 \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{17}{6}. \end{align}

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=\sin{x}.$

Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. If we rotate the graph $180^\circ$ around the origin, we get the same picture. This means that $\sin{x}$ is an odd function, and we have \[ \sin(-x) = -\sin x. \]

Therefore, \begin{align*} \sin(-a) & = -\sin{a} \\[5pt] & = -0.72. \end{align*}
